title: Essentialism
author: Greg McKeown
blurb: Greg McKeown argues that most of us are stretched thin, saying yes to too many things and making only small progress in a million directions. His answer is Essentialism: the disciplined pursuit of less, but better. An Essentialist accepts that we cannot have it all, so they deliberately choose the few things that matter most. The book is built around three stages. First, explore: create space to think, gather information and separate the vital few from the trivial many. Second, eliminate: cut the nonessentials, including learning to say no gracefully and walking away from commitments that no longer serve you. Third, execute: build systems, routines and buffers so that doing the essential things becomes almost effortless. The result is more clarity, more control and more meaningful contribution in work and in life.

lessons.b: Instead of spreading your energy across many things, an Essentialist channels it into the few that matter most, making far more progress where it counts.
Success brings more options and requests, which can scatter our focus and quietly undermine the very clarity that made us successful.
